title: From Sustainability to Regeneration: A Scoping Review of Nursing Practices in the Construction of Green and Healthy Hospitals
content: Background/Objectives: The healthcare sector is responsible for an estimated 1–5% of the global environmental footprint, and hospitals concentrate a large share of that impact through resource consumption, waste generation and greenhouse-gas emissions. As the largest professional group and the staff in closest contact with patients and clinical resources, nurses are pivotal to the transition toward green and, ultimately, regenerative hospitals. This review aimed to identify and synthesise the sustainable nursing practices currently implemented in hospitals and to characterise the role of nursing in reducing the environmental footprint of care. Methods: A scoping review was conducted following the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology and reported in accordance with the PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, SciELO and Dialnet were searched for studies published between 2021 and 2026, complemented by grey and institutional literature retrieved through the institutional library catalogue and by citation searching and hand-searching of key journals. Records were screened independently and in duplicate by two reviewers against predefined eligibility criteria; consistent with scoping-review methodology, no formal quality threshold was used to exclude studies, and the evidence was charted and grouped into six thematic categories aligned with the review objectives. Results: Twenty-five studies were included. Waste management emerged as the domain most sensitive to nursing action, whereas energy and water use were only minimally nurse-sensitive. Education, leadership and the active engagement of nurses were the enablers most consistently reported, while insufficient training, resistance to change and limited investment were the recurrent barriers. Conclusions: Embedding sustainable practices in nursing reduces the environmental impact of hospitals while preserving quality of care and optimising resource use. Nurse-sensitive environmental indicators and the integration of sustainability competencies into curricula and hospital governance are key levers for the transition toward regenerative hospitals.
